reason: Hidden tests call html_writer::react_component() and a fixture implementing the \core\output\react_component_renderable interface (get_react_component_name/get_react_component_props), none of which the issue names; the agent instead added a \core\output\react_component class with render() and a react_renderable interface (get_react_component/export_props_for_react), so both test files die with undefined method/interface. The agent's output is the same data-react-component/data-react-props div, and its render() hook sits after render_<classname> and before named_templatable exactly as required. The only observable differences (JSON_HEX_* escaping, no JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES, array-only props) are unspecified by the issue and are what the html_writer tests assert against.

The failing assertions hard-code the developers' checksum formula: password_verify(hash('sha256', secret . userid.'|'.sortedscopes.'|'.expiry), token), require scopes to be stored sorted ('alpha mid zeta', 'core_course:course:read core_grades:grade:read'), and require a missing token id to raise invalid_api_token_exception instead of dml_missing_record_exception. The issue only asks for bin2hex(random_bytes(32)) and binding scopes+expiry into the hashed secret; the agent does both (HMAC-SHA256 over json of scopes+expiry keyed by the secret, verified in validate_token), so tampering with scopes or expiry is detected. Sorting, the userid in the checksum and the exception unification are extra design choices not in the issue text.

test_get_users_in_report_extrafields_display_custom_profile_field asserts $result['extrafieldsdisplay'][$index] === 'Fruit'; the agent returns the identical server-resolved labels (via \core_user\fields::get_display_name) under the key 'extrafieldlabels' and consumes that key in user.js, so the test fails only on the array name. The second hidden test (duplicate identity fields in the overview table SQL) already passes before and after both patches and is unrelated to the issue. The agent's behaviour removes the raw get_string('profile_field_fruit') call as the issue asks.

The agent only adds the $course = get_site() fallback, but the test test_question_catetory_delete_safe_orphaned still errors because question_save_from_deletion -> question_move_questions_to_category calls context::instance_by_id($question->contextid) without IGNORE_MISSING for the deleted context and throws when creating the question_moved event (the human patch adds the IGNORE_MISSING + context_system fallback). So with the agent's patch the CLI script still fails on exactly the orphaned categories the issue is about: the goal (script repairs orphaned categories) is not achieved, independent of any test naming.

All 15 new tests call course_navigation methods the developers added or made public: get_adjacent_section(), is_first_navigable(), is_last_navigable(), get_all_section_cms() and get_section(); the agent left course_navigation untouched (those helpers stay private/non-existent) and put equivalent logic into footer_content::is_first_activity()/is_last_activity() with private helpers, so the tests error on undefined/private methods. The agent's footer hides previousurl for the first navigable activity and replaces nexturl with a courseurl 'Go to course' link for the last, skipping hidden cms, labels, hidden sections and walking subsections, which is the behaviour the issue asks for. The issue specifies no API, so the failure is an API-location mismatch.

The hidden test file instantiates mod_bigbluebuttonbn\local\admin\setting_configmultiselect_tags (a new tag-style admin setting class with load_choices/write_setting/resolve_label) which the issue never mentions, so every test fatals on the agent's patch. The agent instead adds a comma-separated 'bigbluebuttonbn_recording_safe_formats_extra' text setting whose values are merged into the recording_safe_formats multiselect choices (plus already-stored values), which does let an admin extend the format list without editing source or locking it in config.php. The design differs but satisfies the issue's stated requirement; the failure is entirely the unnamed new class.
